readings.heading: Ὁ Ἀπόστολος — Romans 15:30–33
verses: 30. Brothers and sisters, I beg you, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the Spirit: wrestle alongside me in your prayers to God for me —
31. that I may be rescued from those in Judea who refuse to believe, and that my service for Jerusalem may prove welcome to the saints,
32. so that, by God's will, I may come to you with joy and be refreshed together with you.
33. May the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

readings.heading: Τὸ Εὐαγγέλιον — Matthew 17:24–18:4
verses: 24. At that time, when they came to Capernaum, the men who collect the two-drachma tax came up to Peter and said: "Doesn't your teacher pay the two drachmas?"

25. "Yes," he said. And when he went into the house, Jesus spoke first, before Peter could say anything: "What do you think, Simon? Who do the kings of the earth collect duty and tax from — from their own children, or from outsiders?"
26. Peter said to him, "From outsiders." Jesus said to him: "Then the children are free."

27. "But so that we do not trip them up, go down to the sea, throw in a hook, and take the first fish that comes up. Open its mouth and you will find a stater — take that and give it to them for me and for you."
1. At that very moment the disciples came to Jesus and asked: "So who is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven?"
2. Jesus called a little child over and stood the child in the middle of them,
3. and said: "I tell you the truth: unless you turn around and become like little children, you will never enter the kingdom of heaven.
4. So whoever makes himself low like this little child — that one is the greatest in the kingdom of heaven."
